recall_prompt: Say how you would find the adjoint and inverse of a two by two matrix.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find |A| and Adj A
steps.margin_note: First mark. For a 2×2 there is a shortcut worth learning: swap the two diagonal entries, and change the sign of the other two. No nine cofactors needed.
steps.memory_tip: The 2×2 shortcut: SWAP the diagonal entries and change the sign of the other two. No nine cofactors.
lines: For a 2×2: swap the diagonal, flip the signs

recall.must_convey: That |A| is found (24, non-zero) and that for a 2×2 the adjoint swaps the diagonal entries and changes the sign of the other two.
accept: find the determinant which is twenty four and for a two by two swap the diagonal and change the signs of the others
the determinant is twenty four and the adjoint swaps a and d and negates b and c
use the two by two shortcut for the adjoint after checking the determinant
determinant twenty four, two by two ki diagonal swap chesi migatha rendu sign marchali
swap the diagonal entries and flip the sign of the off diagonal ones

steps.why: The 2×2 shortcut IS the general cofactor rule, worked out once. Knowing it saves the whole cofactor calculation on every 2×2 you meet.
common_mistakes: Swapping the off-diagonal entries instead of the diagonal ones.
Changing the sign of the diagonal entries.

steps.label: Divide by |A|
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Divide every entry by 24 and simplify each fraction: 6/24 = 1/4, 3/24 = 1/8, −4/24 = −1/6, 2/24 = 1/12.
steps.memory_tip: Divide every entry by 24 and simplify each fraction separately.

recall.must_convey: That A⁻¹ is the adjoint divided by |A| = 24, with each fraction simplified.
accept: divide the adjoint by twenty four and simplify each fraction
A inverse is one over twenty four times the adjoint
divide every entry by the determinant to get the inverse
adjoint ni twenty four tho divide cheste inverse vasthundi
the inverse has quarter, one eighth, minus one sixth and one twelfth

steps.why: A⁻¹ = (Adj A)/|A| for every size. The 2×2 case is not a different rule, only a faster route to the adjoint.
